title: Countries & institutions
description: Define the countries and institutions of an exercise, the catalogue of expected actions, and the mandate registry that the gap rules rely on.
noCountriesHint: Create the first country, then its institutions.
cannotDeleteHint: “{{name}}” is referenced by an exercise or another record and cannot be deleted. Archive it instead: it stays in past exercises but disappears from new ones.
codeHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore (max 32). Cannot be changed later.
registryReviewHint: Until an institution's registry is “reviewed complete”, an absent mandate can never be described as a documented gap: gaps are downgraded to inferred.
noMandatesHint: Add mandates by hand with a source from a knowledge base, or import a CSV.
importCsvHint: Imported rows start as “proposed”. Run a dry run first.
actionsHint: What a situation requires. Actions authored by the scenario designer are flagged in reports: they are never an official institutional obligation.
label: Label
importActionsHint: Columns: code,label,domain,derivation,justification,reference_note. Existing codes are skipped. Do this BEFORE importing mandates: a mandate can only cite an action of the catalogue. Run a dry run first.
guideTitle: How to use the mandate registry (and what to do next)

guide.s1: Import or enter the mandates: they arrive “proposed”. A proposed mandate is not yet documented.
guide.s2: For each mandate you can justify: open it, pick a base, search for the passage of the text (article) and click “Use as source”.
guide.s3: Click “Validate” only on mandates that have a source that really exists. Without a source found, validation is refused.
guide.s4: Leave the others “proposed” (or “rejected” if wrong). That is normal: it is not an error, and it keeps the analysis honest.
guide.s5: Registry review: only set an institution to “reviewed complete” if a person actually examined its list of mandates and judges it complete. Otherwise leave “unreviewed” or “partial”.
guide.s6: Next: create the agents then their access to the bases (Prepare menu). The readiness warning “registry not 'reviewed_complete'” is expected until the review is done.
guide.statusTitle: The three review states of an institution
guide.unreviewed: unreviewed: nobody examined its mandates. A missing mandate will never be called a documented gap.
guide.partial: partial: part was examined, not all. Gaps stay “inferred”.
guide.reviewed_complete: reviewed complete: a human examined the whole registry for the intended period and scope. The only state that allows a “documented” gap. Never use it to make a warning disappear.
guide.counterTitle: Why keep one mandate “proposed” in the demonstration?
guide.counter: Mandate CM-L15 is used for the counterfactual test: while it is not validated, the analysis reports a gap; once its source is added and validated, a NEW exercise no longer reports it. The exercise already played never changes.

sourcesHelp: Pick the knowledge base, search for the passage that grounds this mandate (an article), click “Use as source”, then “Save sources”. Then close and click “Validate”: validation requires a source that really exists in the base.
institutionCountryHint: An institution belongs to a country: its mandates and its agent attach to it.
searchLangHint: Most bases hold French texts: search with words from the text itself (not the mandate description, often in English). Several words from the passage work better than one.
searchNoHit: No passage found: try other words from the text, in its own language, or change the base.
